findings.ACCEPTANCE TEST: Unit/integration test: configure a single-label hostname to resolve to a public IP (e.g., 203.0.113.10) via DNS search suffix; the Spoolman URL validation must reject HTTP for that hostname and require HTTPS.
findings.AREA: Spoolman HTTP URL validation / Network security
findings.CONSEQUENCE: A user entering a single-label hostname such as 'spoolman' could have cleartext Spoolman credentials/API data sent to a non-local public host if DNS resolution points outside the local network, defeating the non-local cleartext mitigation.
findings.EVIDENCE: Remediation states: 'HTTP Spoolman URLs are now accepted only for loopback, private/link-local IPs, .local names, and single-label LAN hostnames; non-local names require HTTPS.' This accepts 'single-label LAN hostnames' based on name shape only. No evidence in the package shows that resolved IP addresses for single-label names are verified before allowing HTTP. The listed host test suites do not include a case where a single-label name resolves to a public IP.
findings.FINDING: The HTTP cleartext Spoolman URL policy still allows any single-label hostname without verifying that its resolved IP address is loopback, private, or link-local. Single-label names can resolve via DNS search domains or malicious DNS to public addresses.
findings.REQUIRED CORRECTION: Before allowing HTTP for any hostname, resolve it and require every resolved IP address to be loopback/private/link-local; otherwise reject HTTP or require HTTPS. Alternatively remove the single-label exception and allow only IP literals in local ranges or .local mDNS names.
